messages:
From: Finovate Ltd <payments@finovate.co>

Subject: Question on settlement currency and fees for invoice 2026-534

Hi Laura,

We received invoice 2026-534 (EUR) and are ready to initiate the wire. A couple of clarifications before we send:

- Our treasury prefers to pay in USD where possible. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept USD and apply the FX on your side so we can remit USD directly?
- If we send USD, what bank details should we use (SWIFT/ABA/Beneficiary name) and will any intermediary bank fees be deducted from the amount due?
- Alternatively, if we send EUR, please confirm whether the advising/intermediary fees will be borne by us (sender) or Redwood (beneficiary). What should we instruct our bank to select for charges: OUR / SHA / BEN?

Attached: invoice_2026-534.pdf (PDF).

We need to close this payment before EOD Fri to meet our month-end. Appreciate a quick confirmation.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Head of Finance — Finovate Ltd
payments@finovate.co

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Finovate Ltd <payments@finovate.co>
Cc: Santander Treasury <treasury@santander-example.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Question on settlement currency and fees for invoice 2026-534

Hi Tom,

Thanks — quick answers below to unblock your treasury:

1) Currency routing options
- We can accept USD remittances and perform the EUR conversion on our side. If you prefer this, please wire the USD gross amount listed in the attached "bank_instructions_redwood.pdf" and mark charges as OUR so beneficiary fees are not deducted from the invoice amount.
- Alternatively, if you wire in EUR, please select SHA (shared) and the intermediary bank charges will be split; in that case please add an extra line to the payment to cover expected correspondent fees (~€12–€25 depending on the US intermediary).

2) Intermediary/beneficiary fee allocation
- OUR: sender pays all intermediary and beneficiary fees. This is the cleanest option for ensuring the full invoice amount reaches Redwood without adjustments.
- SHA: fees are split; you may see a small deduction on our side. If you choose SHA and want to guarantee full-net settlement, please increase the remittance by the estimated intermediary fee.

3) VAT/tax and invoicing implications
- The invoice is for cross-border professional services. For EU VAT, Finovate (as a B2B customer) should apply reverse-charge where applicable; invoice shows VAT-exempt net amount with our VAT ID for reference. Any FX adjustment surcharge we add to match the net EUR received will be listed as a separate line item and treated consistently with the original service tax treatment.

I cc'd Santander Treasury with the beneficiary SWIFT for reference (they are our bank partner for USD routing).

If you confirm which route you prefer (USD OUR or EUR SHA), we'll send the final wire instructions and a small pro forma showing the FX assumptions so you can approve.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Finance Lead, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0199

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-03T13:40:00Z
Subject: Internal: Finovate payment — fee handling and small FX surcharge proposal

Marissa / Rafael,

Looping you both in. Finovate wants to pay either USD (we accept) or EUR. Two items for decision:

- Do we absorb small intermediary deductions if client chooses SHA, or should we push the client to OUR? My recommendation: insist on OUR for USD remits; if EUR SHA chosen, request the client add a "correspondent fee" line to guarantee full-net settlement.

- FX surcharge: if they wire USD and we convert, we should apply the actual bank-converted FX and list a separate "FX adjustment" line (ref DL-7823). This keeps tax/VAT treatment aligned to the original service line. Rafael — can finance prepare a single-line pro forma that shows: invoice net EUR, USD amount at assumed FX, estimated bank margin, and final EUR expected? We can share that with Tom to approve.

Time-sensitive: they requested EOD Fri. If we want to be flexible on OUR vs SHA for long-term relationship, we can offer to accept SHA once and invoice the small deduction as a one-off credit. But prefer clear guidance now.

Thanks,
Laura

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: Santander Treasury <treasury@santander-example.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

Preferred option (recommended): USD remittance, charges OUR
- Instruct your bank to send USD to the account below and select OUR so intermediary/beneficiary fees are paid by you. That ensures Redwood receives the full invoice-equivalent EUR.
- Account name: Redwood Inference, Inc.
- Beneficiary bank: Santander (NY)
- SWIFT: SANUS33XXX
- ABA (USD): 026009593
- Account number: 123456789
- Reference: INV 2026-534 / DL-7823

If you must send EUR (secondary option):
- Instruct SHA; please add an extra correspondent fee line of €20 to cover typical intermediary deductions. If you select SHA and do not add a cover amount, we will apply an "FX adjustment" credit or debit on the next invoice to reconcile the shortfall.

VAT/tax note: the original invoice is B2B and treated under reverse-charge where applicable. Any FX adjustment we create will be listed as a discrete line and will follow the same tax treatment.

Next steps for you
- Confirm preferred route (USD OUR or EUR SHA + €20 cover)
- Send remittance advice to payments@redwood.ai once sent

Internal note: Rafael will issue the small pro forma showing USD/EUR conversion and the expected EUR net post-conversion; we will not finalize until we receive remittance advice.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — let me know if you want us to accept SHA once as a courtesy and apply a credit; otherwise OUR keeps reconciliation simplest.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
